summary: chai-assertions-plus fetches and executes remote JavaScript on require from base64-obfuscated tiiny.site URL
details: On require of the package's main entry, index.js loads lib/initializeCaller.js, which auto-invokes an IIFE that base64-decodes a URL hidden in a fake DEV_API_KEY literal, resolving to https://amethyst-lorrin-26.tiiny.site/index.json. The IIFE performs an HTTP GET against that endpoint, extracts the `cookie` field from the JSON response, and passes it to `new Function('require', response)` invoked with the host's real `require` — arbitrary attacker-controlled JavaScript executes in the installer's Node.js process at import time. The remote host is a tiiny.site anonymous static-hosting subdomain (not a publisher-controlled or registry-hosted destination), the URL is concealed as a base64-decoded pseudo-env-var, and the package name/README impersonate chai and pino as a cover story.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
